events.title: IEEE International Workshop on Machine Learning for Signal Processing (MLSP)
events.description: Statistical learning and signal processing, including generative models, multimodal learning, and biomedical applications. [Venue: Centennial Hall](https://mlsp26.ieeesps.org/getting-to-the-conference/).

events.title: Georgia Statistics Day
events.description: Research talks and student posters connecting the regional statistics community; 8 a.m.–5:30 p.m. Keynote speaker: Jianqing Fan.

events.title: Emory AI for Health Symposium
events.description: The fourth symposium on AI in medicine and health, at 1760 Haygood Drive NE.

events.title: NeurIPS 2026 — Atlanta satellite
events.description: Main-conference sessions and tutorials run December 9–11; workshops follow December 12–13. See the [venue information](https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2026/VenueInformation) and the [official list of 26 Atlanta workshops](https://blog.neurips.cc/2026/08/10/announcing-the-neurips-2026-workshops/). Topics include uncertainty-aware decisions, evaluation of agents, reliable clinical simulation, and biomolecular design. Sydney hosts the main meeting December 6–12, while Atlanta and Paris have their own local programs.

events.title: World Models for High-Stakes Health
events.description: NeurIPS Atlanta workshop. Clinical-trial simulation, treatment-effect estimation, causal inference, and uncertainty quantification using longitudinal patient data; rooms C208–C209.

events.title: Agentic Intelligence for Medical Imaging and Multimodal Clinical Data (AIM-NeurIPS)
events.description: NeurIPS Atlanta workshop. AI agents that combine medical images, clinical records, and analysis tools, with an emphasis on evaluation, reliability, and human oversight.

events.title: Generative and Experimental Perspectives for Biomolecular Design (GEM)
events.description: NeurIPS Atlanta workshop. Generative models, active learning, and experimental validation for proteins, molecules, and nucleic acids; relevant to computational biology and drug discovery.

events.title: Machine Learning & the Physical Sciences
events.description: Hosted by the AI4Science Center, this independent workshop connects machine learning with physical-science research. It is near the NeurIPS venue but is not an official NeurIPS workshop in 2026. Virtual participation is available; NeurIPS registration is not required.

events.title: Suddath Symposium
events.description: Experimental, computational, and AI approaches to predictive biomedical models, drug development, and toxicity assessment. Venue: Petit Biotechnology Building, Suddath Seminar Room 1128.

events.title: APHL ID Lab Con
events.description: An applied public-health laboratory conference with tracks on pathogen genomics, infectious-disease outbreaks, and surveillance. The March 15 Advanced Molecular Detection workshop covers metagenomic sequencing, bioinformatics workflows, and genomic epidemiology.

events.title: SIAM Conference on Applications of Dynamical Systems (DS27)
events.description: Includes data-driven and AI-informed dynamical systems, stochastic dynamics, and scientific applications. The travel-support deadline follows SIAM’s [dedicated travel-award page](https://www.siam.org/conferences-events/conference-support/travel-and-registration-support/).

events.title: ACM Federated Computing Research Conference (FCRC)
events.description: Co-located computing conferences connect statistical modeling, learning theory, simulation, and computing systems. See STOC, SIGMETRICS, and SIGSIM-PADS below. [SPAA](https://spaa.acm.org/) and [PLDI](https://conf.researchr.org/home/pldi-2027/) also participate in FCRC week; check their programs for individual dates.

events.title: STOC 2027
events.description: Part of FCRC. Theory of computation, including a day on theoretical computer science and AI.

events.title: SIGMETRICS 2027
events.description: Part of FCRC. Measurement, statistical modeling, and performance analysis of computing systems.

events.title: SIGSIM-PADS 2027
events.description: Part of FCRC. Simulation methods and systems for modeling complex processes.

events.title: UGA Statistics Industry Day
events.description: Statistics and industry connections, featuring Shan Ba; Caldwell Hall, Room 204.

events.title: Georgia State Graduate Conference for Research, Scholarship and Creative Activity
events.description: Graduate research from all disciplines, with presentations and opportunities to connect across departments. Abstract submission for this edition has closed.

events.title: Kennesaw State Fall Analytics Day
events.description: Student analytics projects and conversations with regional industry practitioners; 8:30 a.m.–12:30 p.m. Free and open to the public.

events.title: Emerging Researchers National Conference in STEM (ERN)
events.description: A broad student research conference. The organizer has announced the 2027 dates; submission requirements for that edition are still being updated.

events.title: ASA DataFest at UGA
events.description: A student data-analysis competition; consult the departmental calendar for participation and venue details.

events.title: Atlanta AI Week
events.description: Sessions and workshops on implementing AI, enterprise applications, and the local startup community.

events.title: AI Connect Expo
events.description: An industry exhibition and conference focused on AI applications and technology providers; the organizer's [event information](https://aiconnectexpo.com/sitemap) lists the dates and venue.

events.title: SLDS 2026: Inference and Intelligence
events.location: Marriott at the Brooklyn Bridge, New York
events.description: Statistical learning and data science. This meeting is outside the Atlanta region. Registration closed early on October 12 because the meeting reached capacity; abstract submission has also closed.

events.title: Atlanta Mathematics of Data Science Bootcamp
events.description: Tutorials and projects on the mathematical foundations of data science and ML, for undergraduate and high-school students.

events.title: ACM AI Leadership Summit
events.description: AI research, agentic systems, governance, and applications across academia and industry.

events.title: STI Prevention Conference
events.description: Applied public-health research on sexually transmitted infections, prevention strategies, and service delivery, connecting researchers with clinical and community partners.

events.title: FOPAM 2026
events.location: Courtyard by Marriott Atlanta Decatur Downtown/Emory, Decatur
events.description: Process and product analytics and machine learning. The [July 26–27 pre-conference workshop](https://dais.chbe.ubc.ca/fopam2026/) connected experimental design and regression with deep learning, LLMs, and AI agents.

events.title: Summer Institute in Statistics and Modeling in Infectious Diseases (SISMID)
events.description: In-person short courses in statistical and infectious-disease modeling, including ML, MCMC, and simulation-based inference; online modules ran June 22–26.

events.title: Atlanta Cloud + AI Conference
events.description: Practitioner sessions on cloud infrastructure, AI applications, RAG, and model deployment. See the organizer's [2026 event packet](https://atlcloudconf.com/assets/pdfs/ATLCloud%2BAIConf2026-SponsorshipPacket.pdf).

events.title: STATGEN 2026
events.description: The ASA Section on Statistics in Genomics and Genetics conference, co-organized by Emory's Department of Biostatistics and Bioinformatics, on statistical methodology for genomic and genetic data.

events.title: 11th Workshop on Biostatistics and Bioinformatics
events.description: Organized by Yichuan Zhao, with research talks and student posters. Yong Chen's May 8 short course covered federated learning for collaborative health research using PDA and the MOSAiC framework.

events.title: CDC Epidemic Intelligence Service (EIS) Conference
events.description: Applied epidemiology, disease investigations, and public-health data analysis. The organizer links to the 2026 agenda, presentation abstracts, and recorded sessions.

events.title: Atlanta AI Week 2026
events.description: Enterprise AI, practical workshops, and startup networking.

events.title: Georgia State Undergraduate Research Conference (GSURC)
events.description: Undergraduate research, scholarship, and creative projects across disciplines.

events.title: INFORMS Optimization Society Conference
events.description: Optimization for data science, decisions under uncertainty, and computational methods.

events.title: Computational Cognition Conference (CoCo Con)
events.description: Computational approaches to cognition and their connections with AI.

events.title: Southeast Regional Clinical & Translational Science Conference
events.location: Callaway Resort and Gardens, Pine Mountain, Georgia
events.description: Georgia CTSA's regional meeting connected clinical and translational researchers. The [2026 program](https://georgiactsa.org/_includes/documents/sections/research/cmdts/2026-conf-agenda-final.pdf) included medical AI implementation, clinical prediction, imaging, and LLM applications.

events.title: Georgia CTSA BERD Research Forum
events.description: The Biostatistics, Epidemiology, and Research Design forum focused on artificial intelligence in medical and health care systems, with research presentations and graduate-student posters.

events.title: ASA/IMS Spring Research Conference
events.description: A regional option beyond Georgia for research in statistics and its applications.

events.title: Design and Analysis of Experiments
events.description: Research on experimental design and analysis.

events.title: UGA Statistics: Yu Wang
events.description: 4:30–5:30 p.m. Statistics departmental research talk. Consult the [department calendar](https://www.stat.uga.edu/events/all) for the latest room and talk details.

events.title: UGA Statistics: Ruoxuan Xiong
events.description: 4:30–5:30 p.m. Statistics departmental research talk. Consult the [department calendar](https://www.stat.uga.edu/events/all) for the latest room and talk details.

events.title: UGA Statistics: Yuke (Andrew) Wang
events.description: 4:30–5:30 p.m. Statistics departmental research talk. Consult the [department calendar](https://www.stat.uga.edu/events/all) for the latest room and talk details.

events.title: UGA Statistics: Qin Lu
events.description: 4:30–5:30 p.m. Statistics departmental research talk. Consult the [department calendar](https://www.stat.uga.edu/events/all) for the latest room and talk details.

events.title: UGA Statistics: Inkoo Lee
events.description: 4:30–5:30 p.m. Statistics departmental research talk. Consult the [department calendar](https://www.stat.uga.edu/events/all) for the latest room and talk details.

events.title: UGA Statistics: Jeffrey Rosenthal
events.location: University of Georgia, Athens; Brooks Hall, Room 145
events.description: 4–5 p.m. Statistics departmental research talk. Consult the [department calendar](https://www.stat.uga.edu/events/all) for the latest room and talk details.

events.title: Georgia Tech ML Seminar: Story of 3 D’s — Deep Image Prior, Diffusion Models, and Deep Linear Networks
events.location: Georgia Tech, Atlanta; CODA 9th-floor Atrium and online
events.description: Noon–1 p.m. Saiprasad Ravishankar (Michigan State) discusses neural approaches to image reconstruction and the dynamics of network training. Visitors need to arrange CODA access with the organizer at least two business days ahead; online access details are on the event page.

events.title: Georgia Tech ML Special Seminar: Advancing Data-driven Science of Meditation for Improved Mental Health
events.location: Georgia Tech, Atlanta; CODA C1315 Grant Park Conference Room and Zoom
events.description: 3–4 p.m. Saiprasad Ravishankar (Michigan State) presents EEG analysis and machine learning for studying meditation and mental health. Visitors need to arrange CODA access with the organizer at least two business days ahead; the event page also provides online access.

events.title: UGA SCC: An Introduction to Handling Missing Data in R
events.location: University of Georgia, Athens; Miller Learning Center, Room 213
events.description: 3–4 p.m. Daniel Hall introduces missing-data mechanisms, imputation, and likelihood-based analysis, with practical examples in R. A Statistical Consulting Center seminar; see the [department calendar](https://www.stat.uga.edu/events/all) for the latest details.

events.title: Georgia Tech Machine Learning Seminar — Session V
events.location: Georgia Tech, Atlanta; CODA 9th-floor Atrium and online
events.description: Noon–1 p.m. The posted research background covers AI for physics, experimental design, and high-dimensional inference; the talk title and abstract are still to be announced. Visitors need to arrange CODA access with the organizer at least two business days ahead.

events.title: Emory: Generative AI in Academic Writing and Research — Promise and Pitfalls
events.location: Emory School of Medicine; check the organizer’s page for attendance details
events.description: Noon–1 p.m. Jon D. Duke presents a professional-development lecture on generative AI in scholarly work. The series is aimed at faculty but welcomes other interested participants; the organizer requests an RSVP.

events.title: Kennesaw State Data Science: Toward Trustworthy Human-AI Teaming through Visual Transparency
events.location: KSU Marietta Campus; Atrium Building, Room J1220
events.description: Rescheduled from October 26 to October 28; the room is now J1220. 2–3 p.m. Jieqiong Zhao (Augusta University) presents visual analytics, trust after AI errors, and ways to combine LLM reasoning with human verification. Open to students, faculty, alumni, staff, and the public.

events.title: Kennesaw State Data Science Colloquium — November
events.location: KSU Marietta Campus; Atrium Building, Room J1050
events.description: 11 a.m.–noon. A research seminar with discussion on data science and related methods. Open to the university community and the public; consult the organizer’s page for the speaker and talk announcement.

events.title: Georgia Tech Machine Learning Seminar — Hal Daumé III
events.location: Georgia Tech, Atlanta; CODA 9th-floor Atrium and online
events.description: Noon–1 p.m. Hal Daumé III (University of Maryland), whose research includes language, fairness, and trustworthy AI. The talk title and abstract are to be announced. Visitors should arrange CODA access with the organizer at least two business days ahead.

events.title: Emory Core Day
events.location: Emory University, Atlanta; Convocation Hall, 505 Kilgo Circle
events.description: Research presentations and networking with shared research facilities across Georgia. The [program](https://www.cores.emory.edu/eicf/core-day/core-day-2026-schedule.html) includes computational brain imaging, AI-related health research, and biostatistics core services. Attendance is free, but advance registration was required by October 23; check with the organizer about any remaining availability. The agenda remains subject to change.

events.title: Georgia Tech Machine Learning Seminar — Enric Boix-Adsera
events.location: Georgia Tech, Atlanta; CODA 9th-floor Atrium and online
events.description: Noon–1 p.m. Enric Boix-Adsera (Wharton) studies how AI models learn, with an emphasis on efficiency and reliability. The talk title and abstract are to be announced. Visitors should arrange CODA access with the organizer at least two business days ahead.

events.title: Georgia Tech IDEaS over Coffee: How Dangerous Are Runaway AI Agents?
events.location: Georgia Tech, Atlanta; IDEaS Suite, CODA 12th floor
events.description: 2–3:30 p.m. An informal discussion of AI-agent safety and security with members of the AI Safety Initiative. Georgia Tech students, faculty, and staff are welcome; the organizer provides reception-area escorts near the start for attendees without CODA access.

events.title: Kennesaw State: Computational Methods for Complex Power-System Decision-Making
events.description: 11:30 a.m.–12:30 p.m. Rui Bo (Missouri S&T) discusses optimization, graph-based learning for power-flow calculations, and decisions involving renewable energy. Part of the engineering college’s research seminar series.

events.title: Emory Living Health: Barry R. Davis — The Preventioneers
events.location: Emory Living Health series; see the organizer’s page for attendance details
events.description: 6–7 p.m. An author Q&A with biostatistician and clinical trialist Barry R. Davis about prevention, public health, and translating evidence into action. Hosted by Emory’s Center for the Study of Human Health with the Georgia Center for the Book; RSVP information is on the event page.

events.title: GSU Distinguished Lecture: Shaping AI for the Public Good & Life Lessons
events.location: Georgia State University, Atlanta; Student Center East, Speaker’s Auditorium
events.description: 5:30–7 p.m. David A. Patterson (UC Berkeley) discusses supporting academic AI research for public benefit and lessons from his career in computing. The K.N. King and Susan A. Cole Distinguished Lecture is hosted by GSU Computer Science; no admission charge is listed.

events.title: GSU Experimental Economics: AI Sycophancy and Decisions
events.location: Georgia State University, Atlanta; 55 Park Place, Room 604
events.description: 3–4:30 p.m. John Conlon presents research on AI sycophancy and decision-making. Hosted by the Experimental Economics Center; the announcement lists students and faculty/staff as its audience.

events.title: GSU: AI-Enhanced Decision-Making
events.location: Georgia State University, Buckhead Center; 3348 Peachtree Road, Atlanta
events.description: 9–11:30 a.m. The first session in the Center for Engaged Business Research’s two-part series examines human judgment, decision quality, and trustworthy AI decision support. The announcement welcomes the public and university community and links to attendance information.

events.title: UGA SCC: Data Analysis with Power BI — Mary Akinde
events.location: University of Georgia Statistical Consulting Center; online via Zoom
events.description: Noon–1 p.m. Mary Akinde introduces data preparation, modeling, calculated measures, and interactive dashboards in Power BI, with examples from applied analytics. The organizer provides the Zoom link and seminar flyer.
